items.context: The new graph endpoint needs a home. The existing overview/ package does similar aggregation but has a different response shape and purpose. The depgraph/ package is a pure graph library. Options for where the new graph projection code lives.

options.label: New internal/graph/ package
options.rationale: Clean separation of concerns. Graph projection is a distinct capability from overview aggregation. Avoids bloating existing packages. Follows screaming-architecture (new bounded context = new module). Recommended because the response format, filtering logic, and SSE integration are all unique to this feature.

options.label: Extend internal/overview/ package
options.rationale: Reuses existing service wiring and data loading. But overview returns a different shape and adding lens filtering would complicate the existing code. Risk of creating a grab-bag module.

items.context: The API has no existing SSE infrastructure. The Operations lens needs real-time push. The broker needs to manage client connections, fan-out events, and handle disconnects. This is the first streaming feature in swarm-manager.

options.label: Dedicated internal/sse/ package with generic broker
options.rationale: Reusable by any future SSE endpoint. Broker manages client set, fan-out goroutine, heartbeat, and cleanup. Graph package calls broker.Publish(event). Clean separation between transport (SSE) and domain (graph events). Recommended because it follows the thin-handler pattern and is reusable.

options.label: SSE handling inline in internal/graph/
options.rationale: Simpler — fewer packages, all graph-related code in one place. But SSE connection management is a transport concern, not a graph concern. Makes the graph package harder to test and less reusable.

options.label: Use a third-party SSE library
options.rationale: Libraries like go-sse handle connection management. Reduces custom code. But adds a dependency, and the broker logic is straightforward enough to implement in ~100 lines.

items.notes: Note that we have set up sse very well in other scenarios before, such as ecosystem-manager

items.context: SSE events need to be triggered when scenario status changes, execution state transitions, or agent run updates occur. The question is how to hook into these state changes without tightly coupling every service to the SSE broker.

options.label: Callback interface injected into services
options.rationale: Define a simple EventDispatcher interface (e.g., Dispatch(event Event)) and inject it into execution service, scenario handlers, etc. Services call dispatcher on state changes. Testable via mock dispatcher. Follows existing adapter/injection patterns in the codebase. Recommended because it's consistent with the existing DI approach.

options.label: In-process event bus (pub/sub channel)
options.rationale: Central event bus that services publish to and SSE broker subscribes to. More decoupled — services don't know about SSE. But adds an intermediary that may be over-engineered for a single consumer. Go channels work but need lifecycle management.

options.label: Polling-based event detection
options.rationale: SSE handler polls execution-runs.json and scenario status periodically. Simplest implementation — no hooks needed. But adds latency (poll interval) and wastes CPU when nothing changes. Goes against the SSE research recommendation.

items.context: BacklogItem → Scenario 'targets' edges are resolved by matching acceptance_allow globs against scenario filesystem paths. Need to decide how scenario discovery and glob matching works at the API level.

options.label: Resolve at graph-build time from scenario catalog
options.rationale: Load the scenario catalog (already available via scenarios service), then for each backlog item with acceptance_allow globs, check which scenario root paths match. Simple prefix matching (e.g., 'scenarios/swarm-manager/**' matches scenario 'swarm-manager'). Fast enough given bounded scenario count (~10-50). Recommended because it's straightforward and uses existing data.

options.label: Pre-compute and cache targets edges
options.rationale: Compute targets mapping on startup or when backlog items change. Avoids recomputation on every graph request. But acceptance_allow changes are infrequent and the computation is cheap, so caching adds complexity without meaningful gain.

The research findings are complete and usable — the execute item can proceed. The plan incorporates all relevant findings from the conclusion.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections. Problem statement, scope, technical context, target end state (response format examples), 4-phase implementation strategy, contract decisions (ID formats, lens params, response envelope, SSE event types), testing plan with 9 test cases, risks with mitigations, and definition of done. Phases cover: (1) data model + projection service, (2) HTTP handler, (3) SSE infrastructure, (4) tests.
